summary:
I built the deterministic email-intelligence library in src/lib/email. All 273 tests in the three email suites pass. The classifier gets 40 of 40 corpus fixtures right (100%), each fixture meets its minimum confidence, and none of the job-alert, unfinished-application or invitation-to-apply fixtures produces an observation. tsc reports no errors in my paths and eslint is clean.

What each part does:
- **Parsing (parse.ts, html.ts):** turns raw .eml, mbox, Gmail raw or Microsoft Graph JSON into one `ParsedEmail`. HTML is converted to readable text, attachments are ignored, and text is capped at 200 KB. A missing or invalid Date header gives `receivedAt: null`; mailparser on its own would substitute the current time. Without a Message-ID the id falls back to a stable sha256.
- **Classification (classify.ts):** weighted phrase rules per class, with explicit precedence. Unfinished applications and invitations to apply are never submissions. Job-alert digests win even when a listing says "application submitted". Offer, rejection, onboarding, interview and assessment beat "thank you for applying". A "received" email from a job board or ATS becomes APPLICATION_SUBMITTED; from the employer it becomes EMPLOYER_ACKNOWLEDGMENT. Forwarded emails are classified by their original sender; quoted replies are ignored. The rules are general phrase families, not fixture strings, and adversarial inputs are covered by the synthetic tests.
- **Extraction (extract.ts, datetime.ts, platforms.ts):** employer, title, requisition, platform, location, pay, interview time, recruiter and application link. Each value must be backed by something in the email, otherwise it stays null; job alerts and unrelated mail get no employer or title.
- **AI hook:** `classifyEmailWithOptionalAi` only asks the AI when deterministic confidence is below 0.6. It never lets the AI turn an alert, unfinished application or invitation into a submission, and caps AI confidence at 0.85. No AI implementation is included.
- **Observations (observation.ts):** maps each class to the ingest contract. The evidence snippet is at most 300 characters around the deciding phrase, with emails, phone numbers and URLs masked.
- **Storage (store.ts):** idempotent per user, provider and message id. Review routing follows your thresholds. The body is stored (URL query strings removed, at most 8 KB) only on rows that need review. Re-runs never change a status the user set to CONFIRMED or DISMISSED. `purgeReviewedBodies` clears

summary:
Built the ingestion engine, the matcher, duplicate scan/merge/dismiss and the /applications/review queue. All Phase 2 acceptance scenarios pass through the real email pipeline and the real engine.

What each part does:
- **Matcher** (`match-score.ts` is pure, `match.ts` queries the DB): checks hard signals first, then a fuzzy score:
  - Hard signals: an explicit id = 1.0; same requisition number and same company = 1.0; same posting URL = 0.98; a linked email thread = 0.97; a saved source link with the same URL = 0.97.
  - Fuzzy score (only when company similarity is at least 0.85): title similarity, location agreement, how close the dates are, and penalties for conflicting requisitions or a different posting on the same site.
  - Every query is scoped to the user, bounded and uses an index.
  - A match needs a score of at least 0.9 and a 0.1 lead over the runner-up; 0.65 to 0.9 goes to review.
- **Engine** (`engine.ts`): one transaction per observation, with a per-user advisory lock (a test confirms two concurrent deliveries for the same new job produce one record).
  - Steps: validate, explicit-id ownership check (follows merged records), evidence first, then match or review.
  - Status changes, field filling, source links and attaching evidence all go through the `*InTx` service functions. XP is awarded only by the service's event recording.
  - Verified platform confirmations create a Confirmed record. APPLY_STARTED never writes anything.
  - Interview invitations write their time onto the INTERVIEW_SCHEDULED event. An Interview row is created only when the evidence is verified (i.e. the user reviewed it).
  - Exports `observationFromCapture` and `observationFromEmailRow`.
  - Two policies beyond the brief:
    1. When the service refuses an unverified *forward* move over a verified stage, the engine returns needs_review instead of silently attaching the email.
    2. Evidence older than the current stage never reopens a closed record.

summary:
Built the integrations registry, adapters, Gmail/Outlook OAuth with sync, the sync endpoint, the /integrations page and the four-tab /applications/import. None of it has been tried against a live provider: Google, Microsoft, Greenhouse and Lever are unreachable from the sandbox, so everything was tested with fake servers. Uploads over 1 MB will fail until next.config.ts raises the server-action body limit (shared change request 1).

- **Registry** (`registry.ts`): one entry per provider plus UNION_PORTALS, each with an honest capability matrix. `computeStatus` returns exactly one status and a reason.
  - Gmail/Outlook are "Manual-only" ("OAuth client not configured — import .eml/.mbox files instead") unless client id, secret and APP_URL are all set. They are "Connected" only with a CONNECTED connection.
  - Every job board and ATS is "Manual-only". Greenhouse and Lever are "Experimental" (posting details only, not live-verified).
  - The Chrome extension is "Connected" only if a non-revoked token was used in the last 30 days.
- **Adapters**: one interface with typed results. Unsupported operations throw `NotSupportedError`. All HTTP goes through an injected fetch.
  - Gmail uses a narrow search query, fetches raw messages and runs them through `processRawEmail("GMAIL")`.
  - Outlook reads Microsoft Graph with the text-body header and follows next links only on graph.microsoft.com. Messages that don't look job-related are dropped before parsing.
  - Both stop at exactly 500 messages per run and resume from a saved cursor. They refresh the token once on a 401, and a revoked grant marks the connection NEEDS_REAUTH. Messages classified unrelated are never stored.
  - Each run writes a SyncRun with counts, error codes (no message content) and a status. It updates `lastSyncAt` / `lastError` and never revives a connection that was disconnected during the sync.
  - Greenhouse and Lever job-details lookups use fixed hosts and validated path segments. Lever does not return the employer's name, so company stays empty for Lever postings.
- **OAuth**: authorization code with PKCE (S256). State and verifier sit in a sealed, 10-minute HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie tied to the current session and user.
  - The callback rejects a wrong state, a different session, expiry, another provider, cancellation, and grants without mail access (those are also revoked).
  - Tokens are stored only encrypted; the tests confirm the plaintext never appears in the database row.
  - Disconne

**Extension API** (`/api/extension/me`, `/lookup`, `/captures`, plus OPTIONS)
- The server matches what `extension/src/lib/api-client.js` and `capture.js` send, including `evidence.captureId`. The extension sends that id on every capture, so rejecting unknown keys would have broken it.
- Auth uses `authenticateBearer` plus a scope check. Bad, revoked or expired tokens and deleted accounts get 401 JSON. A missing scope gets 403. Each token is limited to 60 requests a minute; after that it gets 429 with `retryAfterSeconds` and a `Retry-After` header.
- Validation is strict: unknown keys are rejected at both levels, URLs are capped at 2048 characters and strings at 300. The page title and confirmation sentence are masked for emails and phone numbers again on the server.
- Preflight returns 204 and only echoes `chrome-extension://` origins or the APP_URL origin.
- POST /captures runs in one transaction under the per-user ingestion lock:
  - **Attach:** if `applicationId` isn't the user's, it returns 404 and stores nothing.
  - **Duplicates:** a repeat of the same kind, URL and confirmation text within 24 h, or the same `captureId` within 7 days, returns the existing capture with action "duplicate".
  - **JOB_PAGE:** ingested as JOB_SEEN, which creates a Saved record or matches an existing one.
  - **APPLY_STARTED:** stored only, as pending.

I built the Electrician Academy learning module: content loading, safe rendering, lessons with server-graded quizzes, a simulated workshop bench, a practice exam and a certification roadmap. tsc is clean for my paths, eslint shows 0 problems, and `npx vitest run tests/unit/academy-*.test.ts` passes (10 files, 96 tests, DB suites included). I could not open it in a browser here; UI is only checked by renderToStaticMarkup smoke tests.

- **Content loader** (`src/lib/academy/content.ts`, server-only): reads the lesson, workshop and question-bank JSON at runtime and validates it with zod (up to 16 sections). It caches per process in production and re-reads on file changes in dev. Invalid files, unknown prerequisites, unsolvable workshop tasks and bad bank questions are skipped and logged, never fatal. The real content loads with zero issues.
- **Safe rendering**: lesson markdown becomes React elements, so raw HTML shows as text. Diagrams go through an allowlist SVG sanitizer right before they are injected. It removes scripts, `on*` handlers, href/xlink:href, external, `data:` and `javascript:` references (also when entity-encoded), `url()` in style, foreignObject, `<use>`, `<image>` and animation. It keeps local `url(#id)` markers and maps the diagrams' five dark-theme colors to the app's theme tokens. Tests prove each removal and that all real diagrams survive unchanged.
- **Lessons and quizzes**: `/academy` shows tracks, per-track progress, lesson cards that stay locked until prerequisites are complete, and Electrician XP and level. A lesson page shows formula cards, diagrams, worked examples revealed step by step, callouts styled by tone, scrollable tables, a practice panel with instant feedback and a link to the quiz. Opening an unlocked lesson marks it IN_PROGRESS. The quiz is graded by a server action. One transaction saves the QuizAttempt and LessonProgress and, on a pass, awards LESSON_COMPLETED XP (key `xp:lesson:<key>`) and calls `applyEventToMissions` and `evaluateAchievements`. Retakes are allowed and XP is earned once.
- **Workshop**: a pure DC solver (open = ∞, short = 0, never NaN) drives a generated schematic and a virtual multimeter. The meter stays blank until the student commits an answer or presses Measure. Numeric tasks are graded with absolute or relative tolerance; fault-finding multiple-choice is graded on the server. Attempts are saved as `workshop:<key>`, no XP is ever awarded, and every screen says "Simulation — not qualifying field

summary: Built the CareerQuest game engine. Missions: a real implementation replaces the registry indirection. A pure catalog (src/lib/game/mission-catalog.ts) generates daily, weekly, Operation Get Hired phase (1/2/3 plus 30-day next-phase blocks) and $150K Electrician Path missions. ensureMissions creates them idempotently on (userId, key, periodStart). evaluateMissionsTx recomputes progress from persisted data on every evaluation (distinct qualified positions, merged excluded; follow-ups one per application per day; lessons, quizzes, work hours, interview prep, résumé versions, target companies, integrations/imports, program interests, certification status, salary scenarios, next-phase plan). Completion sets COMPLETED and completedAt, awards XP once (dedupeKey xp:mission:<id>), and increments PlayerStats.missionsCompleted and DailyActivity.missionsCompleted once. Rest days skip and restore today's dailies; a reported job pauses job-search missions; expired missions just expire. Anti-farming: cumulative and self-check campaign missions are earned once ever, and a superseded run's open missions expire. Streaks (F4 fixed): pure computeStreak (rest days and non-workdays neither break nor extend, grace for fewer than 5 planned workdays, today never breaks) plus touchStreak, called from awardXp. Levels and derived 0-100 stats with formulas shown in the UI; refreshPlayerStats writes the PlayerStats columns. 23 achievements in a pure catalog; evaluateAchievements is a real implementation that unlocks once and returns only new unlocks. UI: /missions (Today), /missions/week, /missions/campaign (timeline, employment, paychecks, plan, Electrician Path) and /missions/achievements (motion unlock animation, reduced-motion aware), a global celebration mounted in the app layout, and TodayMissionsCard for the dashboard. Server actions all use requireUser, a rate limit, zod and revalidatePath. Notes in docs/notes/game-engine.md.

Nothing was opened in a browser; the UI is only covered by render tests.

One thing blocks real use: uploads go through server actions, which Next limits to 1 MB by default. Files between about 1 MB and 10 MB will fail until next.config.ts is changed (first shared change request). The forms check the 10 MB limit before sending and show an error message if the server refuses the upload, rather than crashing the page.

- **Seed:** `prisma/seed.ts` loads the 6 programs and 5 certification requirements from data/seed. It never deletes rows or touches user data. **Career Map (/career-map, ?node=<key> opens a stop)**
- **The map:** 26 stops. The main electrician path runs Beginner → Entry preparation → Trainee or Apprentice → Supervised experience → Certification eligibility → California certification (DIR) → Experienced electrician → Specialist / Foreman / Management.
- **Three separate credentials:** "Apprenticeship completion (journeyman)" is its own stop. It is one of two alternative routes into Certification eligibility (the other is supervised hours). The CSLB C-10 license branches from Experienced electrician. The page says none of the three automatically grants the others.
- **Side branches:** elevator, commercial HVAC, industrial maintenance, building engineer, construction office (coordinator → estimator → assistant PM) and plumbing & pipefitting. Each starts with an entry-route stop.
- **Where the numbers come from:** every electrician-path figure (hours, fees, program lengths, the C-10's 4 years) is read from the data/seed and data/research files. Each figure shows its source links, check date and any Unverified / Conflicting / Partially verified flag. The C-10 years are parsed from the seed text.
- **No invented numbers:** CareerQuest's own wording contains no figures, side branches are descriptions only and say so, and durations are labelled Estimate. A validator and the tests enforce this. If a seed file is missing, its figures are left out rather than guessed.
- **How each stop's status is worked out:** from real records. These are the profile, program applications, certification-tracker dates, verified vs self-reported hours (classroom hours kept apart), Academy lessons and practice exams, and applications matched to stops by job title. Uploaded document types are also used.
- **Evidence:** every status says why, e.g. "In progress because: 1,240 verified hours of 8,000 (General Electrician)". Each piece of evidence is labelled Verified, Self-reported, Observed, Estimate or Marked by you.

summary:
Wrote scripts/validate-academy.mjs, a plain Node validator with no dependencies. It checks every content rule in the brief, solves every workshop circuit numerically, checks the seed data against the research file, and flags known-wrong California facts in all text. Then I fixed the content until it passed: 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit code 0.
